notes: §1985:VI.6.12.2 prints "ENTER language-name-1 [ routine-name-1 ] .", and §1985:I.1.5.2.5.5 says "An implementation of Standard COBOL may include the ENTER statement or not, at the option of the implementor"; WiseOwl takes the option not to provide it (kb/Work PB5308, docs/conformance 3.7.1, GnuCOBOL refuses it), so the format conforms by being refused by name. enterStatement/enterOperand/routineName parse the format so StatementBinder.BindStatementCore reaches BindEnter, which refuses every ENTER with COBOL7240 (DiagnosticCatalog.EnterStatementNotProvided); the PB5178-era period and routine-name arms the prior PARTIAL named are moot with the statement refused (answers kb/Work PB5539 for this row). Probed at --std 85 (classes b, c): ENTER COBOL., ENTER FORTRAN SUB1., ENTER inside IF, ENTER FORTRAN FREE. and ENTER without a period before another statement are each refused with COBOL7240; ENTER with no operand, a literal or three words are syntax errors; at --std 2002 VisitEnterStatement adds the removal COBOL0902 (the double report is kb/Work PB5538). The witness refuses ENTER COBOL. between two DISPLAYs at 85. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5308 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07-refute.json).
